name: Longbows and Crowns: England and France at War
description: A dispute over the French crown ran from 1337 to 1453, through plague and revolt, Agincourt and Joan of Arc, and led to the Wars of the Roses and the Tudors.

checkpoints.name: Two crowns, one map
checkpoints.note: The Plantagenet kings of England also held lands in France, which kept the kings of England and France in dispute. The Kingdom of England and the Kingdom of France grew into rival states.

checkpoints.name: War and plague
checkpoints.note: The Hundred Years' War began in 1337. English archers with the longbow won famous victories, cannon appeared on battlefields, and the Black Death reached England in 1348.

checkpoints.name: Anger and poetry
checkpoints.note: In 1381 the Peasants' Revolt rose against a new tax and its leaders were put down. Geoffrey Chaucer wrote The Canterbury Tales in these years and captured the voices of English society.

checkpoints.name: Agincourt to Castillon
checkpoints.note: Henry V won at Agincourt in 1415. Joan of Arc helped relieve Orleans in 1429, but was captured and tried by an English-backed Church court, and the war ended in 1453 with France in control of almost all its land.

checkpoints.name: The Wars of the Roses
checkpoints.note: England's nobles fought the Wars of the Roses. Richard III died at the Battle of Bosworth Field in 1485, and Henry VII founded the House of Tudor. In the same years Gutenberg's press started to spread printed books.
